deep.reconstruction:
Context: the next page is dated 1832 (Sept., reduction of oscillations, i.e. magnetometer/pendulum work), and the previous page is headed 'Darstellung von I für Kreis in O.st' and holds a harmonic analysis with cos k / sin k coefficients up to k = 12. This page (fol. 107) is the raw table behind that analysis: a calibration of the reading points of a divided circle.

(1) Header geometry. There are four reading points (verniers or microscopes) I, II, III, 0. When I reads z, II sits at z+270°, III at z+90° and 0 at z+45°.

(2) Constant offsets. For the series of Nov. 3 ('Kreis in O[st]'):
- II−I = −5'19.8"
- III−I = −1'54.2"

For the series of Nov. 20 ('ebenso', same arrangement):
- II−I = −5'18.7" (a sign was struck out and rewritten)
- III−I = −1'54.0"

The two series reproduce the offsets to about 1". So the reading points are not at exactly 90°/270° separation; these mean offsets are removed before tabulating.

(3) Main table. For z = 0°, 15°, …, 345° (24 equidistant settings), Gauss lists the residual readings in arc-seconds of I, II and III: first for Nov. 3 (left block), then for Nov. 20 (right block). Presumably these are taken relative to the reference point 0 after the constant offsets are removed (my inference).

Each column sums to nearly zero, which is consistent with residuals about the mean (my check):
- Nov. 3: ΣI = −2.35, ΣII = +0.5, ΣIII = −0.25 over 24 values.
- Nov. 20: ΣI = −1.15.

The two dates agree closely in pattern, so the deviations are systematic (division/eccentricity-type errors), not random. Typical features are:
- maxima near z = 15–45°, 195° and 300°;
- minima near 90–120° and 270°.

(4) Purpose. The 24 equidistant values allow a trigonometric (Fourier) representation f(z) = Σ_{k=0}^{12} (a_k cos kz + b_k sin kz). This is what the previous page carries out with its α, β, γ, δ = α−γ, ε = 2β bookkeeping and its logarithmic computation of a_k, b_k. The aim is to model the periodic graduation errors and reading-point eccentricities of the circle.

The previous page's coefficients do not reproduce directly from column I of either series. My check of Nov. 3, col. I gives a1 ≈ 1.61, a2 ≈ 2.63, b2 ≈ 0.96, against −1.392, 2.920 and 0.788 there. So the analysed quantity is presumably some combination of columns or series, which cannot be fixed from this page alone.
errors: No computational errors are detectable on this page; it is a data table.
The Nov. 20 II−I entry has a struck-out sign/character before 5'18"7; it should be −5'18.7", consistent with Nov. 3 (−5'19.8").
The row label '225' appears overwritten (looks like 245 corrected to 225); the 15° sequence requires 225.

results.what: Calibration of a divided circle by four reading points (offsets 0°, 270°, 90°, 45°), with tabulated residual readings at 24 equidistant settings in two independent series (Nov. 3 and Nov. 20); constant reading-point offsets II−I ≈ −5'19", III−I ≈ −1'54"
results.modern_name: Graduation-error / eccentricity determination of a divided circle via multiple reading microscopes
results.usually_credited_to: Standard 19th-century observatory practice (Reichenbach-era instruments; Bessel's systematic treatment of division errors, 1810s–1820s)

results.what: Preparation of 24 equally spaced values for trigonometric interpolation up to the 12th harmonic (carried out on the previous page)
results.modern_name: Discrete Fourier / harmonic analysis of periodic instrumental errors
results.usually_credited_to: Bessel (division errors), Gauss (trigonometric interpolation, Theoria interpolationis c. 1805), Lagrange/Clairaut earlier

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine observational calibration table of a circle's reading points. Gauss's use of trigonometric interpolation for instrumental errors is well known; nothing mathematically novel is on this page.

checkable.asserts: Nov. 3 column I sums to −2.35 (near-zero residuals)
a2 for Nov. 3 column I ≈ 2.63 (compare 2.920 on the previous page; they differ, so a different combination was analysed)
The II−I offsets from the two dates differ by 1.1 arcsec

transcription_corrections: Header: 'Kreis in 0/1' is better read 'Kreis in O.st' (Ost), matching the previous page's heading.
'Nov. 20 i eben 10' is better read 'Nov. 20 ebenso'.
Nov. 20 II−I: the struck character before 5'18"7 is a corrected sign; the value is −5'18.7".
Header line 'I z' should be read as reading point I at z (the 'z' is the setting variable, not a numeral 2 as in the previous page's margin transcription).
